1.title: Resilience and Recovery
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Resilience and Recovery. It covers the exam area Security Architecture. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The goal. Recovery sites. Platform diversity and redundancy. Backups. Testing, planning and metrics. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Architecture (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: The goal
1.text: The goal. Resilience keeps services running when something fails; recovery brings them back after an outage or attack. Both protect availability (the "A" in C I A).

1.title: Recovery sites
1.text: Recovery sites. Hot site. State: Fully equipped and running, data kept current. Recovery speed: Minutes to hours. Cost: Highest. Warm site. State: Equipment ready, data needs restoring. Recovery speed: Hours to days. Cost: Medium. Cold site. State: Empty space with power and connectivity. Recovery speed: Days to weeks. Cost: Lowest. Also consider environmental factors (power, cooling, floods, location) when choosing a site.

1.title: Recovery sites, continued
1.text: Recovery sites. The figure shows this: Hot, warm and cold sites compared by readiness, speed and cost. Exam tip: Hot equals fastest and most expensive; cold equals slowest and cheapest; warm equals in between. The choice follows the recovery time objective.

1.title: Platform diversity and redundancy
1.text: Platform diversity and redundancy. Platform diversity. Use different vendors, hardware and virtualization so one flaw or outage does not hit everything. Load balancing. Spreads traffic across servers. Clustering. Servers work together and take over if one fails. Autoscaling. Adds or removes capacity automatically with demand. High availability (H A). Design with no single point of failure. Multicloud systems. Run across more than one cloud. Power. U P S (battery), redundant power supply (R P S), generator, surge protector. Storage. raid and replicated storage. Exam tip: U P S bridges a short outage; a generator covers a long one. Clustering gives automatic failover; load balancing shares load and can remove failed nodes.

1.title: Backups
1.text: Backups. Retention. How long backups are kept (legal and business needs). Immutability. Backups that cannot be changed or deleted for a set time: protect against ransomware. Scope. What is backed up: full, incremental (changes since the last backup of any type), differential (changes since the last full). Restoration testing. Test restores regularly: an untested backup is not a backup. Offline and offsite copies. Keep a copy away from the network and in another place. A common rule is three to two-one: three copies, on two types of media, one offsite.

1.title: Testing, planning and metrics
1.text: Testing, planning and metrics. Testing. Failover tests, simulation and parallel processing (run the recovery system alongside production). Disaster recovery (D R). Restore I T systems after a major event. Business continuity (B C). Keep the business running during and after a disruption. Capacity planning. Ensure enough people, technology and infrastructure for the future.

1.title: Testing, planning and metrics, continued
1.text: Testing, planning and metrics. R T O (recovery time objective). Maximum time a system can be down. R P O (recovery point objective). Maximum data loss measured in time (how old the last backup may be). M T T R (mean time to repair). Average time to fix a failure. M T B F (mean time between failures). Average time a system works between failures.

1.title: Testing, planning and metrics, continued
1.text: Testing, planning and metrics. The figure shows this: R T O and R P O on a timeline around an outage. Exam tip: R T O equals how long down. R P O equals how much data you can lose. If backups run every four hours, the R P O is up to four hours. Higher M T B F is better; lower M T T R is better.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors must resume operations within one hour after a disaster and can afford a fully equipped duplicate site. Which site fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Hot site. A hot site is fully equipped and current, giving the fastest recovery.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company backs up every six hours. What is the best description of its R P O? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Up to six hours of data could be lost. The R P O is the amount of data loss tolerated, which depends on the backup interval.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which backup feature helps most to protect against ransomware that tries to delete backups? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Immutability. Immutable backups cannot be changed or deleted for a set time, so ransomware cannot destroy them.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A data center loses power for twenty seconds before the generator starts. Which device keeps servers running in that gap? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: U P S. A U P S provides battery power for short outages until the generator takes over.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which test runs the recovery environment next to production without switching users to it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Parallel processing. Parallel processing runs the recovery system alongside production to check it without disruption.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team measures the average time a server runs before it fails. Which metric is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: M T B F. Mean time between failures is the average operating time between failures.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which recovery site is cheapest and slowest? Answer: A cold site. Question two. What does R T O measure? Answer: The maximum time a system may be down. Question three. What does R P O measure? Answer: The maximum acceptable data loss in time.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between disaster recovery and business continuity? Answer: D R restores I T systems; B C keeps the business running. Question five. What is platform diversity? Answer: Using different vendors or platforms so one failure does not affect everything. Question six. Why test restores? Answer: To prove that backups actually work.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Sites: hot (fast, costly), warm (middle), cold (slow, cheap). Redundancy: load balancing, clustering, autoscaling, H A, multicloud; U P S, R P S, generator, surge protector. Backups: retention, immutability, scope (full, incremental, differential), restoration testing. Plans and tests: failover, simulation, parallel processing; D R versus B C; capacity planning. Metrics: R T O (downtime), R P O (data loss), M T T R (repair time), M T B F (time between failures). In the next module, we continue the course.
